The word shall indicates mandatory requirements strictly to be followed in order to conform to the standard and from which no deviation is permitted (shall equals is required to). 6,7

The word should indicates that among several possibilities one is recommended as particularly suitable, without mentioning or excluding others; or that a certain course of action is preferred but not necessarily required (should equals is recommended that).
The word may is used to indicate a course of action permissible within the limits of the standard (may equals is permitted to).
The word can is used for statements of possibility and capability, whether material, physical, or causal (can equals is able to).
clause:1.4 1.4 Background bookmark:clause:1.4 1.4 Background

6 The use of the word must is deprecated and cannot be used when stating mandatory requirements, must is used only to describe unavoidable situations. 7 The use of the word will is deprecated and cannot be used when stating mandatory requirements, will is only used in statements of fact.

This document defines the interface between federates (simulations, supporting utilities, or interfaces to live systems) and the underlying software services that support interfederate communication in a distributed simulation domain.

The High Level Architecture (HLA) has been developed to provide a common architecture for distributed modeling and simulation (M&S). To facilitate interfederate communications, HLA federates interact with an underlying software infrastructure. This specification defines the standard services and interfaces to be used by the federates to support efficient information exchange when participating in a distributed federation execution. (A federation execution occurs when sets of federates are brought together to support an objective.)

This document is being developed to define the HLA interface specification. The HLA requires a language- independent specification (LIS) and multiple language bindings to support intersimulation communication in a distributed simulation domain.

18 17 hla-body The formal definition of the M&S HLA comprises three main components: the HLA framework and rules specification (found in IEEE Std 1516™-2025), the HLA federate interface specification (found in this document), and the HLA object model template (OMT) (found in IEEE Std 1516.2™-2025). This standard, IEEE Std 1516.1-2025, provides a complete description of the essential elements of the second component of the HLA, the interface specification. 8

clause:1.4.1 1.4.1 HLA federation object model (FOM) framework bookmark:clause:1.4.1 1.4.1 HLA federation object model (FOM) framework
8 Information on references can be found in Clause 2.

The HLA is an integrated architecture that has been developed to provide a common architecture for M&S. The HLA requires that interfederate communications use a standard application programmer's interface (API). This specification defines the standard services and interfaces to be used by the federates in order to support efficient information exchange when participating in a distributed federation execution. Additionally, the capability for reuse of individual federates that adhere to these standard services and interfaces is increased.

This document provides a specification for the HLA functional interfaces between federates and the runtime infrastructure (RTI). The RTI provides services to federates in a way that is analogous to how a distributed operating system provides services to applications. These interfaces are arranged into seven basic service groups, and an eighth group of support services, as follows:

The eight service groups describe the interface between the federates and the RTI and between the federates and the software services provided by the RTI for use by HLA federates. The RTI requires a set of services from the federate that are referred to as ``RTI-initiated'' and are denoted with a (printer's dagger) after the service name.

A concise and rigorous description of the object model framework is essential to the specification of the interface between federates and the RTI and of the HLA services. The rules and terminology used to describe a FOM are described in IEEE Std 1516.2-2025. A simulation object model (SOM) describes salient characteristics of a federate to aid in its reuse and other activities focused on the details of its internal operation. As such, a SOM is not the concern of the RTI and its services. A FOM, on the other hand, deals with interfederate issues and is relevant to the use of the RTI. FOMs describe the set of object classes and interaction classes chosen for a planned federation along with the attributes of the object classes and parameters of the interaction classes.

Every HLA object instance is an instance of an object class found in the FOM. Object classes are chosen by the object model designer to facilitate an appropriate organizational scheme. Each object class has a set of attributes associated with it. An attribute is a distinct, identifiable portion of the object's state. In this discussion, ``attribute designator'' refers to the attribute, and ``attribute value'' refers to its contents. From the federation perspective, the set of all attribute values for an object instance shall completely define the state of that instance. Federates may associate additional state information with an object instance that is not communicated between federates, but this action is outside the purview of the HLA FOM.

19 18 hla-body hlafixedpage 90 69.79 432 9.96 12 Federates use the state of the object instances as one of the primary means of communication. At any point during a federation execution, at most one federate or the RTI shall have the privilege to update the value of a given object instance attribute. A joined federate that has the privilege to update values for an instance attribute is said to own that instance attribute. There are specific (MOM) instance attributes that are owned by the RTI. In some cases, an instance attribute may be unowned, neither owned by a federate nor the RTI. The Ownership Management services allow joined federates to gain ownership of unowned instance attributes, exchange ownership of instance attributes, or release ownership of instance attributes (possibly to become unowned). The federate provides instance attribute values to the other federates in the federation execution via Object Management services. The federate providing the instance attribute values is said to be updating that instance attribute. Federates receiving those values are said to be reflecting that instance attribute.

90 213.78 432 9.96 12 Each object instance shall have a designator. The value of an object instance designator shall be unique for each federation execution. Object instance designators shall be dynamically generated by the RTI.
90 249.78 432 9.96 12 The FOM framework also allows for interaction classes for each object model. The types of interactions possible and their parameters are specified within the FOM.

90 285.78 432 9.96 12 A federation is the combination of a particular FOM, a particular set of federates, and the HLA services. A federation is designed for a specific purpose using a commonly understood FOM and a set of federates that may associate their individual semantics with that object model. A federation execution is an instance of the Create Federation Execution service invocation and entails executing the federation with a specific FOM and RTI and using various execution details.

20 19 hla-body hlafixedpage 90 69.79 432 9.96 12 The arguments to the services described in this document will use different views of the entities depending on a particular RTI implementation. For clarity, the first 11 clauses of this document refer to only a generic view, known as a ``designator,'' when referring to these entities, and the API annexes refer to the actual implementation-specific arguments. Clause 12 ties the two concepts together.

90 129.78 432 9.96 12 Some of the arguments to the services described in this document are in the form of a group that represents some association. These groupings can take several forms (depending on the requirements of the respective service), each of which is described below. The groupings may be implemented slightly differently in each API, but all implementations shall support the same semantics. These groupings are pairs, sets, collections, constrained sets of pairs, and collections of pairs. Collections are sets that permit duplication of elements. They are used in cases in which duplication is unlikely and not really an error. As such, using a collection rather than a set retains the same effects, but without the expensive checks to eliminate duplicates that using a set would require. In these cases, it is preferred not to penalize the majority of users with the less efficient set just to catch errors that are anticipated to be infrequent.
90 249.78 432 9.96 12 The following data are needed for the implementation of a running RTI and federation executions:

90 267.78 432 0 FOM Document Data (FDD): FOM information (e.g., class, attribute, parameter names) used by the RTI at runtime. Each federation execution needs FDD. FDD is provided to the RTI starting with the Management Object Model (MOM) and Initialization Module (MIM) and FOM modules specified in the Create Federation Execution service invocation. FDD will also be provided by the MIM that is automatically provided by the RTI or optionally provided in the Create Federation Execution service invocation. Additional FDD may be provided as joining federates specify additional FOM modules.
90 363.78 432 9.96 12 The following data may be needed for the implementation of a running RTI and federation executions:
90 381.78 432 0 RTI initialization data (RID): RTI vendor-specific information needed to run an RTI. If required, RID are supplied when an RTI is initialized.

90 417.78 432 9.96 12 For all joined federate-initiated services in this specification (except 4.2, 4.5, 4.6, and 4.11), an implied supplied argument is a joined federate's conjointment with a federation execution. For all RTI-initiated services, an implied supplied argument is also a joined federate's connection to a federation execution. The manner in which these arguments are actually provided to the services is dependent on the RTI implementation and the particular API programming language; therefore, it is not shown in the service descriptions. Also, for the RTI-initiated services, some implicit preconditions are not stated explicitly because the RTI is assumed to be well behaved. For many RTI-initiated services, the ``Federate is joined'' precondition presumes the ``Federate is connected'' precondition.

21 20 hla-body hlafixedpage 90 69.79 432 6 Supplied arguments: arguments supplied to the service Returned arguments: arguments returned by the service. Preconditions: conditions that shall exist for the service to execute correctly. Postconditions: conditions that shall exist once the service has executed correctly. Exceptions: notifications of any irregularity that may occur during service invocation. Wherever possible (excepting situations like RTI internal error), exceptions are side-effect free. Exceptions are listed in order of increasing precedence. That is, if the conditions for more than one exception are met simultaneous, the RTI shall throw whichever of those exceptions comes later in the exception list. Reference state charts: reference to state chart(s) that are germane to the service.

39 38 clause:4 4. Federation management bookmark:clause:4 clause:4.1 4.1 Overview bookmark:clause:4.1 hla-body hlafixedpage 90 69.12 300 12 14 4. Federation management
90 126.79 432 9.96 12 Federation management refers to the creation, dynamic control, modification, and deletion of a federation execution.

90 162.79 432 9.96 12 Before any interaction can take place between a federate and an RTI, such as creating a federation execution or joining, the unjoined federate shall perform a Connect to the RTI. When a federate has resigned and has no further intent to join or create federation executions, it shall perform a Disconnect .

90 210.78 432 9.96 12 The exact manner in which RTI-initiated services (callbacks) are invoked on a federate by the RTI is programming-language specific. However, the HLA defines two callback models that govern when callbacks may be invoked. The two callback models are: IMMEDIATE and EVOKED. In the IMMEDIATE model, the RTI shall invoke callbacks immediately when they are available, unless the callbacks have been disabled using the Disable Callbacks service. In the EVOKED model, callbacks are only made when the federate calls the Evoke Callback/Evoke Multiple Callbacks services, unless callbacks have been disabled using the Disable Callbacks service. RTIs shall implement both callback models. The callback model is specified as an argument to the Connect service.

Resign Federation Execution service shall indicate the requested cessation of federation participation. Once a federate resigns from the federation execution, its federate designator shall not be reused in the same federation execution. Before resigning, ownership of instance attributes held by the joined federate should be resolved. The joined federate may transfer ownership of these instance attributes to other joined federates, unconditionally divest them for ownership acquisition at a later point, or delete the object instance of which they are a part (assuming the joined federate has the privilege to delete these object instances). As a convenience to the joined federate, the Resign Federation Execution service shall accept an action argument that directs the RTI to perform zero or more of the following actions: 100.020 463.804 11.160 9.96 12.00 — 121.980 463.804 400.020 9.96 12.00 Unconditionally divest all owned instance attributes for future ownership acquisition. This action shall place the instance attributes into an unowned state (implying that their values are not being updated), which shall make them eligible for ownership by another joined federate. See Clause 7 for a more detailed description. 100.020 514.803 11.160 9.96 12.00 — 121.979 514.803 400.021 9.96 12.00 Delete all object instances for which the joined federate has that privilege (implied invocation of the Delete Object Instance service). 100.020 541.803 11.160 9.96 12.00 — 121.979 541.803 400.021 9.96 12.00 Cancel all pending instance attribute ownership acquisitions. The use of this directive may interfere with the intended semantics of negotiated instance attribute ownership divestiture by allowing instance attributes divested in this way to be unowned (because the cancellation directive may not succeed). 90.001 601.802 433.343 9.96 12.00 { If a federate invokes this service with either directive 1, 4, or 5 as listed in 4.12.1, then for each instance attribute that becomes unowned as a result, if no joined federates are in either the Acquiring state or the Willing to Acquire state with respect to the specified instance attribute, the RTI shall try to identify other joined federates that are willing to own the instance attribute. Ownership management 101.363 7.1 Overview 90.000 126.786 432.000 9.96 12.00 Ownership management is used by joined federates and the RTI to transfer ownership of instance attributes 90.000 138.785 432.000 9.96 12.00 among joined federates. The ability to transfer ownership of instance attributes among joined federates shall 90.000 150.785 432.000 9.96 12.00 be required to support the cooperative modeling of a given object instance across a federation. Only the 90.000 162.785 432.000 9.96 12.00 joined federate that owns an instance attribute shall 100.021 177.785 421.979 9.96 12.00 — 121.981 177.785 400.019 9.96 12.00 Invoke the Update Attribute Values service to provide a new value for that instance attribute 100.021 192.785 421.979 9.96 12.00 — 121.981 192.785 400.019 9.96 12.00 { Receive invocations of the {Provide Attribute Value Update } service for that instance attribute } 100.021 207.784 421.979 9.96 12.00 — 121.981 207.784 400.019 9.96 12.00 { Receive invocations of the {Turn Updates On For Object Instance } and Turn Updates Off For } 121.981 219.784 400.019 9.96 12.00 { {Object Instance } services pertaining to that instance attribute } 90.000 243.784 432.000 9.96 12.00 Figure 16 depicts the ways that ownership of a single instance attribute may be established from the 90.000 255.784 432.000 9.96 12.00 viewpoint of a given joined federate. This diagram is complete insofar as all transitions shown represent 90.000 267.783 432.000 9.96 12.00 legal operations, and transitions that are not shown represent illegal operations. The RTI shall generate 90.000 279.783 432.000 9.96 12.00 exceptions if illegal operations are invoked. 90.000 303.783 432.000 9.96 12.00 An instance attribute shall not be owned by more than one joined federate, and an instance attribute may be 90.000 315.783 432.000 9.96 12.00 unowned by all joined federates. 176 175 clause:8 8. Time management bookmark:clause:8 8.1 1 Overview 8.1.1 2 Logical Time hla-body hlafixedpage 90.000 69.120 432.000 12.00 14.00 8. Time management 97.403 8.1 Overview 90.000 122.766 432.000 9.96 12.00 The time management services and associated mechanisms provide a federation execution with the means to 90.000 133.805 432.000 9.96 12.00 order the delivery of messages throughout the federation execution. Use of these mechanisms permits 90.000 144.785 432.000 9.96 12.00 messages sent by different joined federates to be delivered in a consistent order to any joined federate in the 90.000 155.765 432.000 9.96 12.00 federation execution that is to receive those messages. This ordering of messages is dependent on an 90.000 166.805 432.000 9.96 12.00 underlying concept of logical time. 90.000 187.804 432.000 9.96 12.00 Logical time in the system being modeled shall be represented in the federation as points along the time axis 90.000 198.784 432.000 9.96 12.00 with an initial and final point. A logical time represents a single point on the time axis. A logical time 90.000 209.764 432.000 9.96 12.00 interval represents the distance between two points on the time axis. A joined federate can associate both 90.000 220.804 432.000 9.96 12.00 itself and some of its activities with logical times. A joined federate’s association with a logical time is 90.000 231.784 432.000 9.96 12.00 referred to as the time position of the joined federate. An association of a joined federate’s activities with 90.000 242.764 432.000 9.96 12.00 logical times is denoted by assigning timestamps to the messages representing those activities. Timestamps 90.000 253.803 432.000 9.96 12.00 and time position are both represented by the same logical time data type and, therefore, can be compared, 90.000 264.783 432.000 9.96 12.00 but they are referenced using different terms in order to help clarify whether a given logical time value 90.000 275.763 432.000 9.96 12.00 applies to a joined federate or to a joined federate’s activities. A logical time interval is a separate data type 90.000 286.803 432.000 9.96 12.00 used by time-regulating federates to specify a lookahead and by the RTI to perform arithmetic operations 90.000 297.783 432.000 9.96 12.00 with logical time values. 90.000 318.783 432.000 9.96 12.00 Each joined federate may advance along the time axis during the course of the execution. Such joined 90.000 329.762 432.000 9.96 12.00 federate time position advances may be constrained by the progress of other joined federates, or they may be 90.000 340.802 432.000 9.96 12.00 unconstrained. 90.000 361.802 432.000 9.96 12.00 Time management is concerned with the mechanisms for controlling the advancement of each joined 90.000 372.782 432.000 9.96 12.00 federate along the time axis. In general, time position advances shall be coordinated with object 89.999 383.762 432.001 9.96 12.00 management services so that information is delivered to joined federates in a causally correct and ordered 89.999 394.801 432.001 9.96 12.00 fashion. 89.999 417.781 432.001 9.96 12.00 A joined federate that becomes time-regulating may associate some of its activities (e.g., updating instance 89.999 429.781 432.001 9.96 12.00 attribute values and sending interactions) with logical times. It shall do so by assigning timestamps to the 89.999 441.781 432.001 9.96 12.00 messages representing its activities; these timestamps correspond to the logical times with which the 89.999 453.780 432.001 9.96 12.00 activities are associated. A joined federate that is time-constrained is interested in receiving the messages 89.999 465.780 432.001 9.96 12.00 representing these activities (e.g., reflecting instance attribute values and receiving interactions) in a 89.999 477.780 432.001 9.96 12.00 federation-wide timestamped order. Use of the time management services allows this type of coordination 89.999 489.780 432.001 9.96 12.00 among time-regulating and time-constrained joined federates in an execution. The coordination is achieved 89.999 501.780 432.001 9.96 12.00 by various constraints on joined federate activities described in this clause. 89.999 525.779 432.001 9.96 12.00 The activities of joined federates that are neither time-regulating nor time-constrained (the default state of all 89.999 537.779 432.001 9.96 12.00 joined federates upon joining a federation execution) shall not be coordinated with other joined federates by 89.999 549.779 432.001 9.96 12.00 the RTI, and such joined federates need not make use of any of the time management services. Such joined 89.999 561.779 432.001 9.96 12.00 federates may, however, optionally place timestamps on the messages representing their activities (e.g., 89.998 573.778 432.002 9.96 12.00 updating instance attribute values and sending interactions) to indicate when these actions occur during the 89.998 585.778 432.002 9.96 12.00 federation execution. In this case, the RTI simply passes the specified timestamp, unchanged, to joined 89.998 597.778 432.002 9.96 12.00 federate(s) receiving the message. 621.638 8.1.1 Logical Time 89.998 645.777 432.002 9.96 12.00 The representation of logical time shall be specified to the RTI via the time representation abstract data type 89.998 657.777 432.002 9.96 12.00 (TRADT) (see 4.7 of IEEE Std 1516.2-2025) and should be documented in the time representation table of 89.998 669.777 432.002 9.96 12.00 the federation execution’s FDD. Federation executions requiring multiple time representations within a 89.998 681.777 432.002 9.96 12.00 single execution (e.g., logical time and wall-clock time values) shall realize this functionality explicitly 89.998 693.776 432.002 9.96 12.00 within their TRADT definition, e.g., by using a “time type” field to differentiate between different types of 89.998 705.776 432.002 9.96 12.00 time values. An RTI shall support the standardized time representations shown in Table 21. hlafixedpage

177 176 hla-body hlafixedpage 90.000 69.786 432.000 9.96 12.00 Logical time values shall be used to represent a federate’s time position and timestamp values. TRADT 90.000 81.785 432.000 9.96 12.00 specific methods shall be used to compare the relative order of one logical time with another and to compare 90.000 93.785 432.000 9.96 12.00 a logical time value with the initial value and with the final value. Similar methods shall be used to add and 90.000 105.785 432.000 9.96 12.00 subtract a value to and from of a TRADT instance of logical time, which enforce compliance with the 90.000 117.785 432.000 9.96 12.00 required logical time properties. 90.000 141.785 432.000 9.96 12.00 Logical time interval (LTI) values shall be used to represent lookahead values and intervals of logical time. 90.000 153.784 432.000 9.96 12.00 There is no concept of a “final” or “largest possible” LTI value, but LTIs shall not be negative. However, 90.001 165.784 431.999 9.96 12.00 TRADT specific methods shall be used to test if an LTI value is zero in addition to those which add or 90.001 177.784 431.999 9.96 12.00 subtract a value to and from an LTI value. 90.001 201.784 431.999 9.96 12.00 The arithmetic operations allowed on logical time values shall be restricted. These restrictions permit 90.002 213.783 431.998 9.96 12.00 TRADTs to be generalized, expressing properties not always present in integer or floating-point numbers. 90.002 225.783 431.998 9.96 12.00 Addition and subtraction shall only be defined when the addend or subtrahend is an LTI. While an LTI can 90.002 237.783 431.998 9.96 12.00 be added to an LTI to produce a new LTI, logical time values can only have an LTI added to them or 90.002 249.783 431.998 9.96 12.00 subtracted from them. Comparison operations: less than, less than or equal to, equal to, equal to or greater 90.002 261.783 431.998 9.96 12.00 than, greater than, and not equal to shall be defined upon logical time values and LTIs, but not between 90.002 273.783 431.998 9.96 12.00 them. Logical time values may include positive and negative values between the initial and final values. No 90.002 285.782 431.998 9.96 12.00 other operations shall be permitted. 90.002 309.782 431.998 9.96 12.00 Logical time has the following notable values: 100.022 324.782 421.978 9.96 12.00 a) 121.972 324.782 400.028 9.96 12.00 initial time value--The point on the time axis for which no other point occurs before it. 100.022 339.781 421.978 9.96 12.00 b) 121.982 339.781 400.018 9.96 12.00 final time value--The point on the time axis for which no other points occurs after it. 90.002 363.781 431.998 9.96 12.00 Similarly, LTI has the following notable values: 100.022 378.781 421.978 9.96 12.00 a) 121.965 378.781 400.035 9.96 12.00 Zero time interval--The distance between two logical time values that are equal. When this logical 121.982 390.781 400.018 9.96 12.00 time interval is added to a logical time T1 the result is a logical time T2 == T1. 100.022 405.780 421.978 9.96 12.00 b) 121.982 405.780 400.018 9.96 12.00 Epsilon time interval--The distance between any two consecutive logical times T1 and T2 (i.e. the 121.982 417.780 400.018 9.96 12.00 set of logical times between T1 and T2 is empty). For some representations of local time (e.g. 121.982 429.780 400.018 9.96 12.00 floating point), the distance may not be the same for all values of T1 and T2. 90.002 453.780 431.998 9.96 12.00 LTIs have unusual properties when implemented upon floating-point numbers. As floating-point numbers 90.002 465.779 431.998 9.96 12.00 become larger the distance between adjacent discrete values becomes larger. Thus, the epsilon time interval 90.001 477.779 431.999 9.96 12.00 depends on the logical time to which it is being added or subtracted. Data distribution management (DDM) 97.403 9.1 Overview 90.000 120.786 432.000 9.96 12.00 DDM services may be used by joined federates to reduce both the transmission and the reception of 90.000 131.766 432.000 9.96 12.00 irrelevant data. Whereas DM services provide information on data relevance at the class attribute level, 90.001 142.805 431.999 9.96 12.00 DDM services add the capability to further refine the data requirements at the instance attribute level. 90.001 153.785 431.999 9.96 12.00 Similarly, whereas DM services provide information on data relevance at the interaction class level, DDM 90.001 164.765 431.999 9.96 12.00 services add the capability to further refine the data requirements at the specific interaction level. Producers 90.001 175.805 431.999 9.96 12.00 and consumers of data communicated between joined federates may use the DDM services to bound the 90.001 186.785 431.999 9.96 12.00 relevance of such communicated data. As a result, the RTI can help recognize the irrelevant data and reduce 90.001 197.765 431.999 9.96 12.00 its delivery to consumers. The relevance of communicating interactions or instance attribute updates is 90.001 208.804 431.999 9.96 12.00 expressed by giving a bounding for relevant communication in a space of user-defined dimensions. Both 90.002 219.784 431.998 9.96 12.00 consumers and producers specify the upper and lower bounds for the relevant portion of that space, and the 90.002 230.764 431.998 9.96 12.00 overlap of producers’ and consumers’ region sets is used to bound relevant communication. 253.665 9.1.1 Definitions for DDM 90.002 277.804 431.998 9.96 12.00 The DDM services shall be based on the following concepts and terms: 100.022 292.804 421.978 9.96 12.00 a) 121.983 292.804 400.017 9.96 12.00 A dimension shall be a named interval of nonnegative integers. The interval shall be defined by an 121.982 303.784 400.018 9.96 12.00 ordered pair of values. The first value is 0 (zero) for every dimension. The second value, which can 121.982 314.764 400.018 9.96 12.00 vary for each dimension, is that dimension’s upper bound as specified in the FDD. 100.021 325.803 421.979 9.96 12.00 b) 121.981 325.803 400.019 9.96 12.00 A range shall be a continuous semi-open interval on a dimension. The interval is defined by an 121.981 337.803 400.019 9.96 12.00 ordered pair of values. The first component of the pair shall be called range lower bound , and the 121.982 349.803 400.018 9.96 12.00 second component shall be called range upper bound . The range upper bound shall be strictly 121.983 361.803 400.017 9.96 12.00 greater than the range lower bound. The minimum possible difference between a range lower bound 121.983 373.803 400.017 9.96 12.00 and a range upper bound shall be 1 (one). 100.023 385.802 421.977 9.96 12.00 c) 121.984 385.802 400.016 9.96 12.00 A region specification shall be a set of ranges. The dimensions contained in a region specification 121.983 397.802 400.017 9.96 12.00 shall be the dimensions of the ranges that are included in the region specification. A region 121.983 409.802 400.017 9.96 12.00 specification shall contain at most one range for any given dimension. Each range in a region 121.983 421.802 400.017 9.96 12.00 specification shall be defined in terms of the bounds [0, the corresponding dimension’s upper 121.983 433.802 400.017 9.96 12.00 bound). 100.023 445.802 421.977 9.96 12.00 d) 121.983 445.802 400.017 9.96 12.00 A region template shall be an incomplete region specification where one or more dimensions have 121.983 457.801 400.017 9.96 12.00 not been assigned ranges. 100.023 469.801 421.977 9.96 12.00 e) 121.984 469.801 400.016 9.96 12.00 A region realization shall be a region specification that is associated with an instance attribute for 121.983 481.801 400.017 9.96 12.00 update, with a sent interaction or with a class attribute or interaction class for subscription. The 121.983 493.801 400.017 9.96 12.00 generic term region may be used in circumstances where a region specification, a region realization, 121.984 505.801 400.016 9.96 12.00 or both apply. 100.024 517.800 421.976 9.96 12.00 f) 121.961 517.800 400.039 9.96 12.00 The RTI shall provide the default region , which is defined as having the range [0, the range’s 121.984 529.800 400.016 9.96 12.00 dimension’s upper bound) for each dimension found in the FDD. The default region shall have all 121.984 541.800 400.016 9.96 12.00 dimensions found in the FDD, regardless of the class attribute or interaction class with which it is 121.983 553.800 400.017 9.96 12.00 associated. The default region realization shall not have a region specification. There shall be no 121.983 565.800 400.017 9.96 12.00 way for a joined federate to refer to the default region. If a joined federate creates a region that has as 121.983 577.799 400.017 9.96 12.00 its dimensions all dimensions found in the FDD and has the range [0, the range’s dimension’s upper 121.983 589.799 400.017 9.96 12.00 bound) for each dimension, this region shall be equivalent to the default region, but it is not the 121.983 601.799 400.017 9.96 12.00 default region. 100.024 613.799 421.976 9.96 12.00 g) 121.983 613.799 400.017 9.96 12.00 A collection of attribute designator set and region designator set pairs shall be interpreted as a set of 121.983 625.799 400.017 9.96 12.00 (attribute designator, region designator) pairs. The interpreted form can be viewed as if constructed 121.983 637.798 400.017 9.96 12.00 in the following manner: 121.983 652.798 400.017 9.96 12.00 1) 142.031 652.798 379.969 9.96 12.00 The interpreted form begins as an empty set of (attribute designator, region designator) pairs. 121.983 667.798 400.017 9.96 12.00 2) 142.040 667.798 379.960 9.96 12.00 For each pair (of sets) in the attribute designator set and region designator set pair collection, 142.024 679.798 379.976 9.96 12.00 create the cross product of the attribute designator set with its region designator set. The result 142.024 691.798 379.976 9.96 12.00 is a collection of (attribute designator, region designator) pairs. The union of all such (attribute 142.024 703.797 379.976 9.96 12.00 designator, region designator) pairs shall be the interpreted form. hlafixedpage

If no value is specified for a switch by the FDD(s) supplied 90.000 390.781 432.000 9.96 12.00 in the Create Federation Execution service invocation, then the RTI will provide default values based on the 90.000 402.781 432.000 9.96 12.00 switches defaults table in IEEE Std 1516.2-2025. Support services are also provided to set the local value of the per federate 90.000 426.781 432.000 9.96 12.00 switches that can be changed dynamically during federation execution. 90.000 450.780 432.000 9.96 12.00 The purpose of the switches is to allow a federate or federation to control certain characteristics of the RTI 90.000 462.780 432.000 9.96 12.00 behavior when specific services are invoked. A basic description of each switch is given in IEEE Std 90.000 474.780 432.000 9.96 12.00 1516.2-2025. Additional descriptions of how the RTI behaves based on switch values are provided 90.000 486.780 432.000 9.96 12.00 throughout this document where appropriate. 245 244 10.1.3 2 Handle Normalization hla-body hlafixedpage 90.000 69.786 432.000 9.96 12.00 The enabling of an advisory switch directs that the RTI shall inform the joined federate, via the appropriate 90.000 81.785 432.000 9.96 12.00 advisory notifications, whenever the conditions covered by that advisory change. The disabling of an 90.000 93.785 432.000 9.96 12.00 advisory switch directs the RTI to cease informing the joined federate of changes in the conditions covered 90.000 105.785 432.000 9.96 12.00 by that advisory. When an advisory switch is disabled, all relevant notifications that would have been 90.000 117.785 432.000 9.96 12.00 delivered to the joined federate shall be lost, i.e., the RTI shall not save the relevant actions and send them to 90.000 129.785 432.000 9.96 12.00 the joined federate when a switch is subsequently enabled. 90.000 153.784 432.000 9.96 12.00 There is, however, one case in which the RTI shall not inform a joined federate when specific conditions 90.000 165.784 432.000 9.96 12.00 covered by an advisory change, even if that advisory switch is enabled. Specifically, even if the Attribute 90.000 177.784 432.000 9.96 12.00 Scope Advisory Switch is enabled, there are some actions a joined federate could take that would cause an 90.000 189.784 432.000 9.96 12.00 instance attribute to go out of scope with respect to that joined federate. Since these changes are a result of 90.000 201.784 432.000 9.96 12.00 the joined federate’s own action and the joined federate knows that the action will cause the instance 90.000 213.783 432.000 9.96 12.00 attribute to go out of scope, no out-of-scope advisory notification shall be given the joined federate. The 90.000 225.783 432.000 9.96 12.00 actions that could cause an instance attribute to go out of scope for the acting joined federate are as follows: 100.020 240.783 421.980 9.96 12.00 — 121.980 240.783 400.020 9.96 12.00 The joined federate acquires ownership of the instance attribute. 100.020 255.783 421.980 9.96 12.00 — 121.980 255.783 400.020 9.96 12.00 The joined federate unsubscribes to the instance attribute’s corresponding class attribute, and it is 121.980 267.783 400.020 9.96 12.00 not subscribed to the instance attribute’s corresponding class attribute with region. 100.020 282.782 421.980 9.96 12.00 — 121.980 282.782 400.020 9.96 12.00 The joined federate unsubscribes with region to the instance attribute’s corresponding class attribute 121.980 294.782 400.020 9.96 12.00 so that it is no longer subscribed to the class attribute (with or without region). 90.000 318.782 432.000 9.96 12.00 These cases are referred to as implicit out-of-scope situations because no out-of-scope advisory notification 90.000 330.782 432.000 9.96 12.00 is generated. 90.000 354.781 432.000 9.96 12.00 Note that if a joined federate unsubscribes with or without region to an instance attribute’s corresponding 90.000 366.781 432.000 9.96 12.00 class attribute, but is still subscribed to that class attribute with some other region, it may or may not have 90.000 378.781 432.000 9.96 12.00 caused the instance attribute to go out of scope (assuming it was previously in scope). Since the joined 90.000 390.781 432.000 9.96 12.00 federate does not know if its removal has caused overlap to be lost with the update region set, in this case the 90.000 402.780 432.000 9.96 12.00 joined federate relies on the RTI to inform it of whether the instance attribute has gone out of scope. Only if 90.000 414.780 432.000 9.96 12.00 the joined federate completely removes all subscriptions (DM and DDM based subscriptions) can it know 90.000 426.780 432.000 9.96 12.00 with certainty that it is causing an implicit out-of-scope situation. 90.000 450.780 432.000 9.96 12.00 For purposes of determining whether the conditions covered by each advisory have changed, when the 90.000 462.779 432.000 9.96 12.00 conditions required for sending each advisory become relevant at a given federate, the initial state of each 90.000 474.779 432.000 9.96 12.00 advisory, as discerned by that federate, is as follows: 100.020 486.779 421.980 9.96 12.00 a) 121.967 486.779 400.033 9.96 12.00 Before a federate begins publishing an object class, the conditions covered by the Object Class 121.980 498.779 400.020 9.96 12.00 Relevance Advisory Switch are assumed to be such that the registration of new object instances of 121.980 510.779 400.020 9.96 12.00 the specified object class is not advised. 100.020 522.779 421.980 9.96 12.00 b) 121.980 522.779 400.020 9.96 12.00 Before a federate begins publishing an interaction class, the interaction class is in the Interactions 121.980 534.778 400.020 9.96 12.00 Turned Off state with respect to that federate (see Figure 13). 100.020 546.778 421.980 9.96 12.00 c) 121.981 546.778 400.019 9.96 12.00 Before a federate becomes the owner of an instance attribute, the instance attribute is in the Updates 121.980 558.778 400.020 9.96 12.00 Turned Off state with regard to that federate (see Figure 15). 100.020 570.778 421.980 9.96 12.00 d) 121.937 570.778 400.063 9.96 12.00 Before a federate knows about an object instance, all of the instance attributes of that object instance 121.980 582.778 400.020 9.96 12.00 are in the Attributes Out-of-Scope state with regard to the federate (see Figure 15). 606.638 10.1.3 Handle Normalization 89.999 630.777 432.001 9.96 12.00 Some types of RTI handles have a normalized value that can be used to construct a point range for the 89.999 642.777 432.001 9.96 12.00 appropriate dimension of that handle type . 89.999 654.776 432.001 9.96 12.00 The normalized handle value like the handle itself is originated by the RTI, federation execution-wide 89.999 666.776 432.001 9.96 12.00 unique, and unpredictable. The normalized handle values shall have no guarantee of continuity (i.e. they are 89.999 678.776 432.001 9.96 12.00 suitable only for a point range). The normalized handle values shall have no guarantee of uniqueness but 89.999 690.776 432.001 9.96 12.00 given two equal handle instances, their normalized values shall also be equal. hlafixedpage

Programming language mappings 90.000 101.363 514.000 10.98 12.30 12.1 Overview 90.000 126.786 514.000 9.96 11.16 The services described in this document to this point have been described in a programming-language- 90.000 138.785 514.000 9.96 11.16 neutral way. This approach was taken because support is provided for multiple programming languages as 90.000 150.785 514.000 9.96 11.16 described in the annexes to this document. This clause (i.e., Clause 12) provides the reader with a mapping 90.000 162.785 514.000 9.96 11.16 from the abstract view from the body of this document (Clause 4 through Clause 11) to the programming- 90.000 174.785 514.000 9.96 11.16 language-specific views in the APIs (Annex B through Annex D). It shall be transparent to the federation 89.999 186.785 514.001 9.96 11.16 and participating federates which API or implementation language a specific federate uses. 89.999 210.784 514.001 9.96 11.16 The mappings described in this clause are Ann 100.019 234.784 503.981 9.96 11.16 — 121.979 234.784 482.021 9.96 11.16 Of designators from Clause 4 through Clause 10 to handles and names in the APIs 100.019 246.784 503.981 9.96 11.16 — 121.979 246.784 482.021 9.96 11.16 From services in Clause 4 through Clause 10 to methods in the APIs 100.019 258.784 503.981 9.96 11.16 — 121.979 258.784 482.021 9.96 11.16 From abstract data types in Clause 4 through Clause 10 to classes or data types in the APIs 90.000 288.383 514.000 10.98 12.30 12.2 Designators 90.000 313.806 514.000 9.96 11.16 As explained in 1.5, designators are a generalization of both names and handles. In most cases, what is 90.001 325.805 513.999 9.96 11.16 referred to as a designator in Clause 4 through Clause 10 has both a name and a handle. Which specific form 90.001 337.805 513.999 9.96 11.16 of a designator is used in the APIs is dependent on the language and service in which it is used. Examine the 90.001 349.805 513.999 9.96 11.16 APIs to see which form is needed, although in most cases, the handle is used. Clause 10 presents services 90.001 361.805 513.999 9.96 11.16 that shall be used to map names to handles and vice versa. 90.001 385.805 513.999 9.96 11.16 Names in most cases (e.g., object class names, attribute names, interaction class names) come from the 90.001 397.804 513.999 9.96 11.16 FDD. As such, they are known ahead of time to all federates. Object instance names, however, are different. 90.001 409.804 513.999 9.96 11.16 These names may be chosen by the registering federate, or they may be created dynamically by the RTI. As 90.001 421.804 513.999 9.96 11.16 such, these names often are not predictable. 90.001 445.804 513.999 9.96 11.16 Handles in all cases are generated by the RTI. In most cases, where the handles correspond to names from 90.001 457.803 513.999 9.96 11.16 the FDD, these handles shall be generated in a repeatable manner. In other words, if two federation 90.001 469.803 513.999 9.96 11.16 executions are created on the same version of the same RTI with the same FDD file, then the handles 90.001 481.803 513.999 9.96 11.16 assigned to the same name shall be the same in each federation execution. This property facilitates saves and 90.001 493.803 513.999 9.96 11.16 restores so that handles, rather than just the names, can be saved by federates. This property does not, 90.001 505.803 513.999 9.96 11.16 however, imply that an RTI assign handles in a manner known a priori to federates. 90.001 529.802 513.999 9.96 11.16 Handles shall be unique in a federation execution. Each federate shall know the same item by the same 90.001 541.802 513.999 9.96 11.16 handle. In other words, the federate registering an object instance shall know it by the same handle as 90.001 553.802 513.999 9.96 11.16 another federate that discovers the object instance. 90.001 577.801 513.999 9.96 11.16 Often during a federation execution, it is useful for federates to send information identifying an item to 90.001 589.801 513.999 9.96 11.16 another federate. For example, one federate may wish to send an interaction to another federate informing it 90.001 601.801 513.999 9.96 11.16 that one particular object instance is of particular importance. To send information identifying an item to 90.001 613.801 513.999 9.96 11.16 another federate, there are two options: send the name of the item, or send the handle of the item. 90.001 637.800 513.999 9.96 11.16 To send a handle as an attribute value or as a parameter value, the handle shall be encoded prior to sending, 90.001 649.800 513.999 9.96 11.16 and it shall be reconstituted by the receiver. The precise means of encoding and reconstituting a handle is 90.001 661.800 513.999 9.96 11.16 described for each API in 12.11.6.4, 12.12.6.4, and 12.13.3.3. However, a handle encoded using any API 90.000 673.800 514.000 9.96 11.16 (e.g., C++) shall be reconstitutable in all APIs. Also, a handle of a given type (e.g., an object instance 90.000 685.800 514.000 9.96 11.16 handle) shall be reconstitutable only as that type. hlafixedpage

424 423 hla-body hlafixedpage 90.000 68.648 514.000 13.98 15.66 Annex E 90.000 97.140 514.000 12.00 13.44 (normative) 90.000 128.648 514.000 13.98 15.66 Rationale 90.000 169.140 514.000 12.00 13.44 E.1 Overview 90.000 195.786 514.000 9.96 11.16 This annex contains additional information that might be useful to explain various aspects of HLA and is not 90.000 207.785 514.000 9.96 11.16 a complete rationale of the HLA. Nothing in this clause is required in an HLA implementation. 90.000 231.785 514.000 9.96 11.16 This annex is organized to match the organization of the main body of this specification, and the subclause 90.000 243.785 514.000 9.96 11.16 numbers in this annex correspond to the subclause numbers of the main body. Note, however, that not all 90.000 255.785 514.000 9.96 11.16 subclauses in the main body have corresponding subclauses in this annex. In other words, text is present in 90.000 267.785 514.000 9.96 11.16 this annex only if additional comments were deemed helpful to understanding the corresponding subclauses 90.000 279.784 514.000 9.96 11.16 in the main body. 90.000 309.383 514.000 10.98 12.30 E.1.4 Background 90.000 334.806 514.000 9.96 11.16 Consideration was given to providing several iterating functions; however, there were found to be serious 90.000 346.805 514.000 9.96 11.16 problems documenting and describing the iterating-based semantics of these services. Additionally, there 90.000 358.805 514.000 9.96 11.16 was a problem with every redaction produced. The candidate definitions of how exceptions were handled 90.000 370.805 514.000 9.96 11.16 and recovered from during the “middle” of an iteration sequence never satisfied a large enough set of users 90.000 382.805 514.000 9.96 11.16 to be acceptable for retention in the specification. Each of the users wanted the behavior to meet their 90.000 394.805 514.000 9.96 11.16 specific application needs, which in most cases were inconsistent and impossible to meet with a common 90.000 406.805 514.000 9.96 11.16 mechanism. As a result, it seemed to make the most sense not to have any iterating services and to let users 90.000 418.804 514.000 9.96 11.16 produce their own aggregate functionality with the exception response semantics they needed. 90.000 454.140 514.000 12.00 13.44 E.4 Federation management 90.000 486.383 514.000 10.98 12.30 E.4.6 118.680 486.383 485.320 10.98 12.30 Destroy Federation Execution 274.379 486.383 329.621 10.98 12.30 service 90.000 511.806 514.000 9.96 11.16 Since there can be no joined federates for the destroy service invocation to succeed, there might be a 90.000 523.805 514.000 9.96 11.16 problem if the federation execution has “zombie” or otherwise uncooperative joined federates. To aid 90.000 535.805 514.000 9.96 11.16 matters in this situation, a joined federate can be resigned by another joined federate via a MOM interaction. 90.000 565.403 514.000 10.98 12.30 E.4.31 124.800 565.403 479.200 10.98 12.30 Query Federation Restore Status 296.341 565.403 307.659 10.98 12.30 service 90.000 590.826 514.000 9.96 11.16 One way to employ federation restore status is for a federation manager federate to not invoke the 491.820 590.826 112.180 9.96 11.16 Restore 90.000 602.825 514.000 9.96 11.16 Complete 128.280 602.825 475.720 9.96 11.16 service until all the other joined federates have successfully completed their restore. In this way, a 90.001 614.825 513.999 9.96 11.16 federation manager federate can “throttle” the restore process as it monitors the restore status. hlafixedpage

425 424 hla-body hlafixedpage 90.000 69.120 514.000 12.00 13.44 E.5 Declaration management (DM) 90.000 101.363 514.000 10.98 12.30 E.5.1 Overview 90.000 126.786 514.000 9.96 11.16 One reason joined federates can subscribe at multiple levels in a class hierarchy is to allow for FOM growth. 90.000 138.785 514.000 9.96 11.16 As a FOM expands, a federate application need not be recoded. It can continue to subscribe at the same 90.000 150.785 514.000 9.96 11.16 levels in the hierarchy while other, “newer” federate applications in the federation can subscribe at the new 90.000 162.785 514.000 9.96 11.16 classes. In addition, if a joined federate subscribes to multiple levels in the class hierarchy, it should 90.000 174.785 514.000 9.96 11.16 generally subscribe to the lowest classes first (and work its way up in the hierarchy) in order to help ensure 90.000 186.785 514.000 9.96 11.16 that object instances are discovered at the most specific type. 90.000 210.784 514.000 9.96 11.16 Some services in the interface specification contain postconditions that are less precise than one would 89.999 222.784 514.001 9.96 11.16 expect. The postcondition for the 229.499 222.784 374.501 9.96 11.16 Subscribe Object Class Attributes 367.379 222.784 236.621 9.96 11.16 service, for example, states only that 89.999 234.784 514.001 9.96 11.16 “the RTI has been informed of the joined federate’s requested subscription.” It does not say that the joined 89.999 246.784 514.001 9.96 11.16 federate is now subscribed to the specified class attributes, nor is a statement to this effect found in any 89.999 258.784 514.001 9.96 11.16 service postcondition. 89.999 282.783 514.001 9.96 11.16 Services with such imprecise postconditions include the following: 100.019 306.783 503.981 9.96 11.16 — 121.978 306.783 482.022 9.96 11.16 Subscribe Object Class Attributes 100.019 318.783 503.981 9.96 11.16 — 121.978 318.783 482.022 9.96 11.16 Subscribe Interaction Class 100.019 330.782 503.981 9.96 11.16 — 121.979 330.782 482.021 9.96 11.16 Commit Region Modifications 242.518 330.782 361.482 9.96 11.16 (old Modify Region) 100.019 342.782 503.981 9.96 11.16 — 121.978 342.782 482.022 9.96 11.16 Subscribe Object Class Attributes With Regions 100.019 354.782 503.981 9.96 11.16 — 121.978 354.782 482.022 9.96 11.16 Subscribe Interaction Class With Regions 89.999 378.782 514.001 9.96 11.16 These services have imprecise postconditions, similar to the postcondition quoted above, because the 89.999 390.781 514.001 9.96 11.16 interface specification allows RTI implementations to decide when to determine whether a message sent by 90.000 402.781 514.000 9.96 11.16 one federate should be received by another federate. One possibility is to broadcast all sent messages and 90.000 414.781 514.000 9.96 11.16 perform filtering at each receiving federate. A more efficient possibility is to perform filtering when the 90.000 426.781 514.000 9.96 11.16 message is sent (in other words, the message is sent only to interested federates) and again at each receiving 90.000 438.781 514.000 9.96 11.16 federate (in case the state of the receiver has changed during transmission). 90.000 462.780 514.000 9.96 11.16 The problem with allowing the latter alternative is that should the receiver add to its subscriptions, that 90.000 474.780 514.000 9.96 11.16 addition cannot be considered to have fully taken effect until the RTI can ensure that messages sent by any 90.000 486.780 514.000 9.96 11.16 federate will take the added subscriptions into account, thus the imprecise postconditions. Subscription 90.000 498.780 514.000 9.96 11.16 additions take effect locally immediately, but there will be some delay before the additions take effect 90.000 510.780 514.000 9.96 11.16 throughout the federation execution. An RTI implementation makes these changes take effect throughout the 90.000 522.779 514.000 9.96 11.16 federation execution as soon as possible, but it will not delay the return of these service invocations until it 90.000 534.779 514.000 9.96 11.16 can guarantee the subscription additions are complete. 90.000 558.779 514.000 9.96 11.16 Since federates can come and go and can add subscriptions at any wall-clock time, the only way the RTI 90.000 570.779 514.000 9.96 11.16 could meet a postcondition asserting that the federate is now subscribed to the specified attributes would be 90.000 582.778 514.000 9.96 11.16 to synchronize the whole federation execution so that it could make that guarantee. This is one of the places 90.000 594.778 514.000 9.96 11.16 in the specification where the desire was to permit more federate asynchronous behavior. This places more 90.000 606.778 514.000 9.96 11.16 responsibility on the federates to make their subscriptions in sufficient wall-clock time for them to have the 90.000 618.778 514.000 9.96 11.16 desired effect in their federation execution. 90.000 642.638 514.000 9.96 11.16 E.5.1.2 Definitions and constraints for object classes and class attributes 90.000 666.777 514.000 9.96 11.16 Item o) in 5.1.2 is a very complex sentence, and it has been suggested that it may be difficult for the reader to 89.999 678.777 514.001 9.96 11.16 parse and understand. This text is an attempt to explain what it means by example. hlafixedpage
